title_english: The Forest Spirit and the Virtuous Eldest Daughter
description: Ancient narrative documented in Pacific Linguistics 565 (p. 410), contrasting the filial obedience, gentle speech, and spiritual protection of a modest eldest daughter with the greed of her boastful cousin when tested by the guardian spirit of the Patkai forest.

full_translation: An elderly widow had two young daughters of very different temperaments. The eldest daughter, Nang Luang, was gentle-hearted, diligent, and revered her mother. One afternoon she walked deep into the quiet Patkai forest to gather dry firewood. The forest spirit appeared in the guise of an exhausted traveller; the girl immediately shared her packed rice. Delighted by her purity and generosity, the spirit bestowed upon her a woven basket filled with pure gold. She carried the blessed gift home, and her family rejoiced in peace, sharing food with the entire village. Virtue and selfless giving are the true golden jewels that illuminate human existence.
title: The Forest Spirit and the Virtuous Eldest Daughter
